dailyInsight.headline: Audit who owns the HTTP cookie jar beneath your agent sessions
dailyInsight.insight: Microsoft Agent Framework’s September 15 Python change rejects response-cookie persistence in internally created HTTP clients. Before adopting it, identify which integrations rely on cookies and which authenticated users share caller-owned clients.
dailyInsight.mechanism: Framework-created MCP, A2A, AG-UI and declarative HTTP clients use a cookie policy with no allowed domains. Connection reuse remains; supplied clients and explicit cookies retain their behavior. Separate agent sessions do not by themselves partition transport or server-side identity.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A shared cookie jar can carry one run’s authentication into another, while removing persistence can break legitimate same-session authentication or affinity. The migration requires an explicit ownership decision.

actions.audience: Teams using Microsoft Agent Framework’s Python HTTP integrations
actions.label: Trace one client across two test users
actions.instruction: In a disposable integration, identify the HTTP client owner and test two distinct users against a simulated cookie-setting service. Inspect outbound cookies, caller-owned client lifetime and protocol-session scope. Confirm the installed build contains the September 15 change before expecting its new default.

receipts.title: Make HTTP cookie persistence explicit
receipts.supports: Internally created clients reject saved response cookies; supplied clients retain behavior and remain caller-owned.

receipts.title: MCP ownership and cookie migration
receipts.supports: Cookie rejection applies within sessions too, preserves explicit cookies and does not partition protocol sessions or server-side state.

confidence.basis: Implementation, public migration documentation and synthetic regression assertions agree on the narrow default change. We did not execute the full integration suite.

dailyInsight.limitation: The newest listed Python release at reporting time, September 10’s 1.18.0, predates this source change. A synthetic regression is not proof of a real exposure, and rejecting cookies is not complete user isolation.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the call if the change is reverted, an affected managed-client path still replays response cookies, or the release adopts a different ownership contract.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a Python release carrying the change and verify both cookie-dependent migrations and two-user protocol-session isolation.
